dedupe_keys.name: geoconnex us hydrologic features knowledge graph and reference features internet of water

description: Geoconnex is open data infrastructure that links US water data from many organisations through persistent identifiers for hydrologic features and a shared knowledge graph. It is run within the Internet of Water Coalition, a group of organisations working with federal, state and local governments on water data infrastructure, and is based on work supported by the U.S. Geological Survey. Coverage: the United States; the reference feature server offers 20 collections, including hydrologic units HU02 to HU12, national and principal aquifers, secondary hydrogeologic regions, reference stream gages, mainstem rivers, reference dams, public water systems, and states, counties, tribal areas, core-based statistical areas, urban areas and places. Format and access: reference features through an OGC API Features server (reference.geoconnex.us) returning JSON, JSON-LD and HTML; the knowledge graph at graph.geoconnex.us for SPARQL queries; an explorer web map for datasets and monitoring locations along mainstem rivers; graph data dumps; and a registration route for partners to publish JSON-LD landing pages that a harvester crawls; free. Licence: the documentation is CC0; data carry the terms of each contributing organisation (not stated per collection on the pages read). Caveats: the query tools and explorer are described as in active development, a general REST API for the graph is only planned, and completeness depends on which organisations have contributed. Simulation uses: joining gauges, dams, public water systems and river networks from different agencies into one topology for network flow, hazard exposure and digital twin work on water systems. Related records: the USGS water data APIs (data-usgs-water-data-apis) provide the monitoring data many reference gages point to.
